content: dicej requested alexcrichton for a review on PR #15336.

dicej opened PR #15336 from dicej:fix-barging-ahead-of-pending-tasks to bytecodealliance:main:

The spec says that new tasks are not allowed to "barge ahead" of earlier calls which have been queued due to backpressure, i.e. they need to wait until the queued calls have started before they can run.

The solution here is to maintain a count of those calls (ConcurrentInstanceState::pending_start_count) and add a was_pending field to GuestCallKind::StartImplicit. When creating a new call, we set was_pending to false. Then, if backpressure requires us to queue the call, we set was_pending to true and increment pending_start_count. GuestCall::is_ready now checks both was_pending and pending_start_count (in addition to backpressure, etc.) to determine whether a task can start or needs to be queued, per the spec. Finally, any time we start or cancel a task with was_pending set to true, we decrement pending_start_count.

Claude found the bug and wrote the test case. I wrote the fix independently. I take responsibility for all of it.

I had thought last night that we needed to call StoreOpaque::partition_pending any time ConcurrentInstanceState::pending_start_count went to zero, similar to how we call it when ConcurrentInstanceState::backpressure goes to zero, but after taking a closer look I remembered that the former will only go to zero _after_ the relevant items have already been removed from ConcurrentInstanceState::pending, so there will be nothing left to remove. Also, the barge-past-waiting-to-enter.wast test is covering the case I thought it was missing by waiting for all subtasks to complete (or be cancelled) before exiting.

:memo: alexcrichton submitted PR review:

One question is that I don't believe this currently handles cancellation, for example this test fails:

<details>

(component
  (component $C
    (core func $backpressure.inc (canon backpressure.inc))
    (core func $backpressure.dec (canon backpressure.dec))
    (func (export "bp-on") (canon lift (core func $backpressure.inc)))
    (func (export "bp-off") (canon lift (core func $backpressure.dec)))

    (core func $task.return (canon task.return))
    (core module $m
      (import "" "task.return" (func $task.return))
      (func (export "f") (result i32)
        (call $task.return)
        (i32.const 0)) ;; CALLBACK_CODE_EXIT
      (func (export "f-cb") (param i32 i32 i32) (result i32) unreachable)
    )
    (core instance $i (instantiate $m
      (with "" (instance
        (export "task.return" (func $task.return))
      ))
    ))
    (func (export "f") async
      (canon lift (core func $i "f") async (callback (core func $i "f-cb"))))
  )
  (instance $c (instantiate $C))

  (component $A
    (import "c" (instance $c
      (export "bp-on" (func))
      (export "bp-off" (func))
      (export "f" (func async))
    ))
    (core module $libc (memory (export "mem") 1))
    (core instance $libc (instantiate $libc))
    (core func $bp-on (canon lower (func $c "bp-on")))
    (core func $bp-off (canon lower (func $c "bp-off")))
    (core func $f (canon lower (func $c "f") async (memory (core memory $libc "mem"))))
    (core func $subtask.cancel (canon subtask.cancel))
    (core func $subtask.drop (canon subtask.drop))
    (core func $waitable-set.new (canon waitable-set.new))
    (core func $waitable.join (canon waitable.join))
    (core func $task.return (canon task.return))
    (core module $m
      (import "" "bp-on" (func $bp-on))
      (import "" "bp-off" (func $bp-off))
      (import "" "f" (func $f (result i32)))
      (import "" "subtask.cancel" (func $subtask.cancel (param i32) (result i32)))
      (import "" "subtask.drop" (func $subtask.drop (param i32)))
      (import "" "waitable-set.new" (func $waitable-set.new (result i32)))
      (import "" "waitable.join" (func $waitable.join (param i32 i32)))
      (import "" "task.return" (func $task.return))
      (global $set (mut i32) (i32.const 0))
      (global $pending (mut i32) (i32.const 0))

      ;; Calls `f`, asserts that the subtask is STARTING, and returns its
      ;; handle.
      (func $start-f (result i32)
        (local $st i32)
        (local.set $st (call $f))
        ;; low 4 bits are the subtask status; 0 = STARTING
        (if (i32.ne (i32.and (local.get $st) (i32.const 0xf)) (i32.const 0))
          (then unreachable))
        ;; the subtask handle is in the bits above the 4-bit status
        (i32.shr_u (local.get $st) (i32.const 4)))

      ;; Cancels the not-yet-started subtask `$h` and drops it.
      (func $cancel (param $h i32)
        ;; 3 = CANCELLED_BEFORE_STARTED
        (if (i32.ne (call $subtask.cancel (local.get $h)) (i32.const 3))
          (then unreachable))
        (call $subtask.drop (local.get $h)))

      (func (export "run") (result i32)
        (local $h1 i32)
        (global.set $set (call $waitable-set.new))
        (call $bp-on)
        ;; first call is queued behind backpressure => STARTING
        (local.set $h1 (call $start-f))
        (call $bp-off)
        ;; second call: queued behind h1 => STARTING
        (call $waitable.join (call $start-f) (global.get $set))
        ;; cancel the call ahead of it; the second call must still run
        (call $cancel (local.get $h1))
        (global.set $pending (i32.const 1))
        ;; CALLBACK_CODE_WAIT (2) on `$set`, which goes in the bits above 4
        (i32.or (i32.shl (global.get $set) (i32.const 4)) (i32.const 2)))

      (func (export "cb") (param $ev i32) (param $h i32) (param $status i32) (result i32)
        ;; 1 = EVENT_SUBTASK
        (if (i32.ne (local.get $ev) (i32.const 1)) (then unreachable))
        ;; 2 = RETURNED
        (if (i32.eq (local.get $status) (i32.const 2))
          (then
            (call $subtask.drop (local.get $h))
            (global.set $pending (i32.sub (global.get $pending) (i32.const 1)))))
        (if (i32.eqz (global.get $pending))
          (then
            (call $task.return)
            (return (i32.const 0)))) ;; CALLBACK_CODE_EXIT
        ;; CALLBACK_CODE_WAIT (2) on `$set`, which goes in the bits above 4
        (i32.or (i32.shl (global.get $set) (i32.const 4)) (i32.const 2)))
    )
    (core instance $i (instantiate $m
      (with "" (instance
        (export "bp-on" (func $bp-on))
        (export "bp-off" (func $bp-off))
        (export "f" (func $f))
        (export "subtask.cancel" (func $subtask.cancel))
        (export "subtask.drop" (func $subtask.drop))
        (export "waitable-set.new" (func $waitable-set.new))
        (export "waitable.join" (func $waitable.join))
        (export "task.return" (func $task.return))
      ))
    ))
    (func (export "run") async
      (canon lift (core func $i "run") async (callback (core func $i "cb"))))
  )
  (instance $a (instantiate $A (with "c" (instance $c))))
  (export "run" (func $a "run"))
)

(assert_return (invoke "run"))

</details>

Specifically if two calls are queued, the first is cancelled, then the second doesn't get to proceed as expected.

A second question, the original bug report this is coming from additionally mentioned that Accessor::poll_ready_for_concurrent_call doesn't take any of this new logic into account, erroneously saying that an instance is ready for a call when it in fact gets immediately queued. Did you want to fix that here, or in a separate PR?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

I'm confused by this comment and the growing boolean expression here -- the is_ready function here is making a deduction about self, this comment is referring to other calls, but only self is considered? How is the state of other calls factored in here?
:memo: dicej submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: dicej created PR review comment:

The state.pending_start_count == 0 clause means "there are no calls waiting in line", and the complete expression (*was_pending || state.pending_start_count == 0) means "if I am waiting in line (or was previously waiting in line before I got the go-ahead), then I have the right to go ahead regardless of who else is also in line; otherwise, if there _is_ anyone in line, I need to get in line too if I want a turn".

Does that help? If so, I can expand the comment.
